# Articles with synced voice narration

## Context

The site (Astro 7, fully static, served from Cloudflare Workers static assets) has no blog yet. Goal: add articles that stay plain static HTML for SEO, plus an optional recording of Sara reading the article, with the sentence being spoken highlighted and scrolled into view.

How it works, and where each part runs:

| Part | Where | What |
|---|---|---|
| Article HTML | build time | MDX content collection, static pages |
| Audio | static asset | `public/audio/<slug>.mp3` |
| Timings | authoring time, once per article, on Sara's machine | `public/audio/<slug>.vtt`, one cue per sentence |
| Sync | browser | native `<track>` cues + CSS Custom Highlight API, ~40 lines of vanilla JS |

No backend, no React island, no new npm dependencies. With JS off or in an old browser it degrades to a normal article with a normal audio player.

Decisions already made: sentence-level sync; timings generated by a local script (Whisper forced alignment).

## Design

**Timings format: WebVTT.** A `<track kind="metadata">` inside `<audio>` makes the browser parse the cues and fire `cuechange` at the right moment, so there is no polling or time lookup to write. The file is human-readable, so a bad timestamp can be fixed by hand. Each cue's text is the sentence it covers.

**Matching cues to the page by text, not by index.** On `cuechange` the script finds the page sentence whose normalized text (lowercase, letters and digits only) equals the cue text, searching forward from the last match. If the article is edited after recording, only the changed sentence loses its highlight; nothing drifts.

**Highlighting without touching the DOM.** Sentences are `Range` objects built with `Intl.Segmenter` (sentence granularity) over each block's text; the active one is set via `CSS.highlights.set('narration', new Highlight(range))` and styled with `::highlight(narration)`. No per-sentence `<span>` wrappers in the HTML, and ranges can cross links and `<em>`.

## Changes

1. **`src/content.config.ts`** (new): `articles` collection, `glob` loader over `src/content/articles/*.mdx`. Schema: `title`, `description`, `pubDate`, `narrated` (boolean, default false), `draft` (default false). Check the Astro 7 content-collection API against the docs before writing.

2. **`src/content/articles/<first-article>.mdx`** (new): one real or sample article to prove the pipeline.

3. **`src/pages/articles/index.astro`** (new): list of non-draft articles, newest first, using the existing `Layout`.

4. **`src/pages/articles/[slug].astro`** (new): `getStaticPaths` from the collection, renders `<Content />` inside `<article class="prose">` (typography plugin is already loaded in `src/styles/globals.css:2`, unused so far). When `narrated`:
   - `<audio controls preload="metadata" src="/audio/<slug>.mp3">` with `<track kind="metadata" src="/audio/<slug>.vtt" default>`.
   - A `<script>` that runs on `astro:page-load` (required because `ClientRouter` is on, `src/components/BaseHead.astro:79`), returns early if there is no narration audio or no `CSS.highlights`, clears any previous highlight, builds sentence ranges for `p, h2, h3, h4, li` (skipping `pre`), sets `track.mode = 'hidden'`, and on `cuechange` highlights the matching sentence and scrolls it to center. Scrolling only happens while playing, and is instant instead of smooth under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
   - `::highlight(narration)` style using the existing `blue-1` theme color at low opacity.
   - `BlogPosting` JSON-LD.

5. **`src/components/BaseHead.astro`** and **`src/layouts/Layout.astro`**: add an optional `type` prop (default `website`, articles pass `article`) replacing the hard-coded `og:type` at `BaseHead.astro:51`, and pass `image` through `Layout` (it is accepted by `BaseHead` but not forwarded today).

6. **`scripts/align.mjs`** (new, Node, no npm deps): `node scripts/align.mjs <slug>`
   - Reads the `.mdx`, strips frontmatter, imports, code fences, JSX and markdown syntax.
   - Splits into sentences with `Intl.Segmenter`, writes one per line to a temp file.
   - Shells out to `stable-ts` (run through `uvx`, needs `ffmpeg`) in align mode with the original line splits kept, output `public/audio/<slug>.vtt`. Confirm the exact flags with `stable-ts -h` at implementation time.
   - Self-check: fails loudly if the cue count differs from the sentence count.

7. **`src/pages/rss.xml.js`** (new): feed of articles using `@astrojs/rss`, which is installed but unused. Add the `<link rel="alternate">` in `BaseHead.astro`.

8. **`public/llms.txt`** and **`src/pages/index.astro`**: add the Articles entry / a link to `/articles`.

## Authoring workflow after this lands

1. Write `src/content/articles/my-post.mdx`.
2. Record, export mono MP3 at about 64 kbps to `public/audio/my-post.mp3` (roughly 0.5 MB per minute).
3. `node scripts/align.mjs my-post`, set `narrated: true`, commit.

## Skipped on purpose

- **R2 for audio**: Workers static assets cap files at 25 MiB, which is about 50 minutes at 64 kbps. Move to R2 when an article exceeds that.
- **Click a sentence to seek**, playback speed control, persistent mini-player across pages: add if wanted.
- **Word-level highlighting**: same pipeline with word cues if ever wanted.

## Verification

- `astro build` succeeds; `dist/articles/<slug>/index.html` contains the full article text and `og:type` `article`; `dist/rss.xml` and the sitemap list the article.
- In the dev preview: play the audio, confirm the highlight moves sentence by sentence and the page follows; seek with the scrubber and confirm the highlight jumps; navigate away and back through a view transition and confirm it still works and no stale highlight remains.
- Mobile width and JS-disabled check: article and player still usable.
- After deploy to a preview: confirm seeking works (range requests pass through `worker.ts` to `env.ASSETS`).

32	1. **`src/content.config.ts`** (new): `articles` collection, `glob` loader over `src/content/articles/*.mdx`. Schema: `title`, `description`, `pubDate`, `narrated` (boolean, default false), `draft` (default false). Check the Astro 7 content-collection API against the docs before writing.
33	
34	2. **`src/content/articles/<first-article>.mdx`** (new): one real or sample article to prove the pipeline.
35	
36	3. **`src/pages/articles/index.astro`** (new): list of non-draft articles, newest first, using the existing `Layout`.
37	
38	4. **`src/pages/articles/[slug].astro`** (new): `getStaticPaths` from the collection, renders `<Content />` inside `<article class="prose">` (typography plugin is already loaded in `src/styles/globals.css:2`, unused so far). When `narrated`:
39	   - `<audio controls preload="metadata" src={`${AUDIO_BASE}/<slug>.mp3`}>` with `<track kind="metadata" src="/narration/<slug>.vtt" default>`. `AUDIO_BASE` is one constant in `src/consts.ts`.
40	   - A `<script>` that runs on `astro:page-load` (required because `ClientRouter` is on, `src/components/BaseHead.astro:79`), returns early if there is no narration audio or no `CSS.highlights`, clears any previous highlight, builds sentence ranges for `p, h2, h3, h4, li` (skipping `pre`), sets `track.mode = 'hidden'`, and on `cuechange` highlights the matching sentence and scrolls it to center. Scrolling only happens while playing, and is instant instead of smooth under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
41	   - `::highlight(narration)` style using the existing `blue-1` theme color at low opacity.
42	   - `BlogPosting` JSON-LD.
43	
44	5. **`src/components/BaseHead.astro`** and **`src/layouts/Layout.astro`**: add an optional `type` prop (default `website`, articles pass `article`) replacing the hard-coded `og:type` at `BaseHead.astro:51`, and pass `image` through `Layout` (it is accepted by `BaseHead` but not forwarded today).
45	
46	6. **`scripts/align.mjs`** (new, Node, no npm deps)
47	   - Reads the `.mdx`, strips frontmatter, imports, code fences, JSX and markdown syntax.
48	   - Splits into sentences with `Intl.Segmenter`, writes one per line to a temp file.
49	   - Shells out to `stable-ts` (run through `uvx`, needs `ffmpeg`) in align mode with the original line splits kept, output `public/narration/<slug>.vtt`. Takes the local recording path as a second argument, since the MP3 no longer lives in the repo: `node scripts/align.mjs <slug> <path-to-mp3>`. Confirm the exact flags with `stable-ts -h` at implementation time.

61	2. Record, export mono MP3 at about 64 kbps (roughly 0.5 MB per minute).

content.text:
The articles section and the narration sync are built and working locally. Two things remain: the R2 bucket does not exist yet, and the Whisper alignment step has never been run.

To answer your original question: it is neither a backend job nor much client code. The audio is a static file, the timings are a small `.vtt` file generated once per article on your machine, and about 60 lines of plain JS in the page do the highlighting.

## What I checked
- **Sync:** on a test article, the spoken sentence is highlighted and the page scrolls with it.
- **Seeking:** jumping forwards and backwards moves the highlight to the right sentence, including list items.
- **Page transitions:** leaving and returning leaves no stale highlight and the sync still works.
- **Build:** `pnpm build` passes; the article gets `og:type` `article`, and appears in `rss.xml` and the sitemap.

The test used a synthesized voice with exact timings, not a real recording.

## What is not done
- **R2 hosting:** production pages point at `https://audio.saranatour.dev/<slug>.mp3`, which does not exist until the bucket and custom domain are created.
- **Alignment script:** `scripts/align.mjs` shells out to `stable-ts` through `uvx`, and `uv` is not installed here. Its text-splitting half is tested; the Whisper call uses the flags from the stable-ts README but has never run.
- **Nothing is committed.**

## Things you might trip over
- **Sample article:** `hello-narration.mdx` is a placeholder marked `draft: true`, so it shows in `pnpm dev` but not in production. Its `.vtt` matches the synthesized test audio; replace both.
- **Local audio:** in dev the player reads from `public/audio/`, which I added to `.gitignore`. A local build still copies those files into `dist/`.
- **Article title:** the `<h1>` is not part of the timed text. If you read the title aloud, nothing is highlighted during it.

## Per-article workflow
1. Write `src/content/articles/my-post.mdx`.
2. Save the recording as `public/audio/my-post.mp3`.
3. Run `node scripts/align.mjs my-post` to write `public/narration/my-post.vtt`.
4. Upload the MP3 to R2 (the script prints the command).
5. Set `narrated: true` and commit.

The main files are [src/pages/articles/[slug].astro](src/pages/articles/[slug].astro), [scripts/align.mjs](scripts/align.mjs) and [src/content.config.ts](src/content.config.ts). I also added an "articles" nav link, an RSS feed, and an Articles line in `llms.txt`.
tell me how it works? does it work for the entire article, does it a sound for it to work?

Yes to both: it covers the whole article, and it needs your recording, because the audio is what drives the highlight.

## How it works

There are three pieces per article:

- **The article text**: ordinary HTML built from your `.mdx` file.
- **Your recording**: one MP3 of you reading the article.
- **A timings file** (`.vtt`): a plain text list saying which sentence is spoken from which second to which second, for example:

  ```
  00:00:04.623 --> 00:00:07.547
  Press play and the sentence being spoken is highlighted.
  ```

When someone presses play, the browser reads the timings file alongside the audio. Each time the audio crosses into a new entry, the page finds the sentence with the same words, highlights it and scrolls it to the middle of the screen. Dragging the audio scrubber jumps the highlight to match.

## Does it cover the entire article?

Yes: every sentence in paragraphs, headings and list items gets an entry. The exceptions are:

- **Code blocks** are skipped, since you would not read them aloud.
- **The article title** at the top is not included, so nothing is highlighted while you read it.
- **Sentences you edit after recording** lose their highlight, because the words no longer match the timings file. The rest of the article stays in sync.

## Does it need a sound?

Yes. Without a recording there is nothing to follow, so the highlighting only exists on articles marked `narrated: true`. An article without audio is just a normal article with no player, which is the default.

You do not write the timings by hand. The script `scripts/align.mjs` listens to your recording, matches it against the article text and writes the file for you. That step is the one part I have not been able to run yet, since it needs `uv` installed.
and how do I release articles after this

Releasing an article means getting its `.mdx` file onto `main` with `draft: false`; the site rebuilds and the article appears in the list, the RSS feed and the sitemap on its own.

## Text-only article

1. Create `src/content/articles/my-post.mdx` with this at the top, then write below it in Markdown:

   ```
   ---
   title: My post title
   description: One sentence for search results and link previews.
   pubDate: 2026-11-25
   draft: true
   ---
   ```

2. Preview it with `pnpm dev` at `/articles/my-post`. Drafts show there but never in production.
3. When it is ready, change `draft: true` to `draft: false`.
4. Commit and merge to `main`, then deploy the way you deploy the site today. I have not checked whether your Cloudflare deploy runs automatically on push or whether you run `wrangler deploy` yourself.

The file name becomes the URL, so `my-post.mdx` is published at `saranatour.dev/articles/my-post`.

## Article with your voice

Do the same as above, plus these steps before step 3:

1. Record yourself reading it and save it as `public/audio/my-post.mp3`.
2. Generate the timings:

   ```bash
   node scripts/align.mjs my-post
   ```

3. Check it in `pnpm dev`: press play and watch the highlight follow.
4. Upload the recording, using the command the script prints:

   ```bash
   pnpm wrangler r2 object put site-audio/my-post.mp3 --file public/audio/my-post.mp3 --remote
   ```

5. Add `narrated: true` to the top of the article.

The MP3 itself is not committed; only the article and the small `public/narration/my-post.vtt` file are.

## One-time setup before the first narrated article

- **Audio hosting:** the R2 bucket and the `audio.saranatour.dev` domain do not exist yet. I can create them when you say so.
- **Alignment tool:** install `uv`, which the timings script needs:

  ```bash
  brew install uv
  ```

- **This work:** the articles feature itself is still uncommitted on the `wire-og-images` branch, so it has to be merged and deployed before any article can go live.
what does uv do?

`uv` is a tool that downloads and runs Python programs without you having to set up Python packages yourself.

Here it has one job. The timings script needs `stable-ts`, a Python program that uses Whisper to listen to your recording and work out when each sentence is spoken. When you run `node scripts/align.mjs my-post`, the script calls `uvx` (a command that comes with `uv`), which fetches `stable-ts` the first time, keeps it in a cache, and runs it.

- **First run:** slow, since it downloads `stable-ts`, its dependencies and a Whisper model, which is likely a few gigabytes in total.
- **Later runs:** it reuses the cache and only does the alignment.
- **Scope:** it runs only on your machine when you generate timings; it is not part of the website or its build.
- **Privacy:** Whisper runs locally, so your recording is not sent anywhere.

The alternative is to install `stable-ts` yourself with `pip3 install stable-ts` and have the script call it directly, but that puts it and its large dependencies into your main Python setup.
is there a simpler way to do that?

Yes: skip Whisper entirely and mark the timings yourself by tapping a key while you listen to the recording once.

## How the tap-along version would work

1. Open the article in `pnpm dev` and press play.
2. Each time you hear yourself start a new sentence, press a key (say, the spacebar). The page highlights the next sentence so you can see where you are.
3. At the end, the page gives you the finished `.vtt` file to save into `public/narration/`.

## How it compares

| | Tap-along | Whisper script (current) |
|---|---|---|
| Installs | none | `uv`, plus a few gigabytes on first run |
| Your time per article | one listen-through | about a minute of waiting |
| Accuracy | as good as your tapping, roughly a quarter second | usually tighter, but can misplace sentences if you ad-lib |
| Fixing a mistake | re-tap, or edit the time in the file | edit the time in the file |

I'd go with tap-along. You will listen to each recording once anyway to check it, so the extra cost is small, and nothing can break on a Python or model update. It is about 30 lines added to the article page, active only in dev.

Two other options exist, and I would not pick either:

- **Hosted transcription API:** no local install, but it costs per article, uploads your voice to a third party, and needs an API key.
- **Paragraph-level timings typed by hand:** no tooling at all, but you lose the sentence-by-sentence highlight you chose.

Say the word and I'll build the tap-along mode and remove the Whisper script.
yes remove the whisper script

content.text:
The Whisper script is removed and replaced with a tap-along mode: you play your recording in `pnpm dev` and press Space as each sentence starts. I checked it in the preview (taps, undo and the saved file all behave) and the build passes with the tap code left out of production.

## Recording timings now

1. Put the recording at `public/audio/my-post.mp3` and set `narrated: true` on the article.
2. Open the article in `pnpm dev` and click **Record timings (dev only)**. The audio starts from the beginning.
3. Press **Space** each time you start a new sentence. The sentence you just marked is highlighted, and **Backspace** undoes a mistap.
4. Click the button again to save. It downloads `my-post.vtt`; move it into `public/narration/` and reload to see the result.

No installs are needed, so `uv` is off the list. Each tap is shifted 0.2 seconds earlier to allow for reaction time; that is one number (`TAP_LAG`) in [src/pages/articles/[slug].astro](src/pages/articles/[slug].astro) if highlights feel late or early.

## About the Web Speech API

It exists, but it is a poor fit here, so I would not use it:

- **It listens to a microphone, not a file.** It is built for live dictation. Newer Chrome versions can reportedly take an audio track as input, but I have not verified that.
- **It gives no timestamps.** You get the recognised words, not when they were spoken. You would have to note when each result arrives, which lags the voice by a varying amount.
- **It returns its own transcript.** That would still need matching against your article text, with misheard words in the way.
- **Browser support is patchy.** Firefox does not support it, and Chrome traditionally sends the audio to Google's servers.

Tapping gives better timing than that with less code.

input.content:
# Publishing an article

One article per pull request. Merging the PR to `main` publishes it: Cloudflare Workers Builds rebuilds the site, and the article shows up on `/articles`, in `/rss.xml` and in the sitemap.

This file lives outside `public/` and `src/pages/`, so it is not part of the website.

## 1. Branch

```bash
git switch main && git pull
git switch -c article/my-post
```

## 2. Write

Create `src/content/articles/my-post.md`. The file name is the URL: `saranatour.dev/articles/my-post`.

```md
---
title: My post title
description: One sentence for search results and link previews.
pubDate: 2026-11-25
draft: true
---

Write the article here in Markdown.
```

`draft: true` keeps it off the live site. Drafts still show in `pnpm dev`, at `localhost:4321/articles/my-post`.

## 3. Narration (optional)

Skip this section for a text-only article.

1. **Record** yourself reading the article. Read the text as written: a sentence you change while reading won't be highlighted. Don't read the title; it isn't part of the timed text.
2. **Export** a mono MP3, about 64 kbps, and save it as `public/audio/my-post.mp3`. That folder is gitignored, so the MP3 never goes into the repo.
3. **Add** `narrated: true` to the frontmatter.
4. **Mark the timings.** In `pnpm dev`, open the article and click **Record timings (dev only)**. The audio plays from the start; press **Space** each time you begin a new sentence, **Backspace** to undo a mistap. Click the button again to save.
5. **Move** the downloaded `my-post.vtt` into `public/narration/` and reload. Press play and check the highlight follows you. To fix one sentence, edit its time in the `.vtt` by hand; to redo the lot, record the timings again.
6. **Upload** the audio:

   ```bash
   pnpm wrangler r2 object put site-audio/my-post.mp3 --file public/audio/my-post.mp3 --remote
   ```

If highlights consistently feel late or early, adjust `TAP_LAG` in `src/pages/articles/[slug].astro`.

## 4. Open the PR

1. Change `draft: true` to `draft: false`.
2. Commit the article, plus `public/narration/my-post.vtt` if it has audio.
3. Push and open a PR titled `Article: My post title`.

Before merging, check:

- [ ] `pnpm build` passes.
- [ ] `draft: false`, and `pubDate` is the day you publish.
- [ ] `description` reads well on its own: it is what link previews and search results show.
- [ ] Narrated: the MP3 is uploaded, and `https://audio.saranatour.dev/my-post.mp3` plays in the browser.

## 5. Merge

Merge to `main`. After the deploy finishes, open the live article and press play.

## Fixing a published article

Edit the `.md` in a new PR. If it is narrated and you changed a sentence, the highlight skips that sentence until you re-record it and redo the timings. To replace the audio, upload the new MP3 under the same name; browsers and the CDN may keep serving the old one for a while.

## Removing an article

Delete the `.md` (and its `.vtt`) in a PR. Optionally delete the audio:

```bash
pnpm wrangler r2 object delete site-audio/my-post.mp3 --remote
```

I took your "read" to mean "write" and your "yes" to mean moving this work onto its own branch; tell me if you meant something else.

**What the guide covers**, one article per PR:
1. Create an `article/my-post` branch.
2. Write `src/content/articles/my-post.md` with `draft: true`.
3. If it has audio: record, save the MP3 locally, tap the timings in dev, move the `.vtt` into place, and upload the MP3 to R2.
4. Set `draft: false` and open the PR. There's a short checklist to go through before merging.
5. Merge to `main`, then check the live page.

It also covers fixing and removing a published article.

**Branch:** the articles work, including the guide, is now on a new `add-articles` branch from `main`. None of it is committed. On `wire-og-images` the local merge commit is still there but was never pushed, and nothing else on that branch is waiting to land.

**Two things to know:**
- The guide says merging to `main` deploys the site. I based that on the "Workers Builds: site" check on your PRs, but haven't confirmed it. That check also failed on PR #83, so it's worth a look in Cloudflare before relying on it.
- The guide's upload step won't work until the R2 bucket and `audio.saranatour.dev` exist. I can set those up whenever you want.
what if I served my articles somewhere else like on github gists or something?

You can, as long as the site pulls the gists in when it builds rather than in the reader's browser. For your setup I'd still keep articles in the repo.

## How it would work

Astro can load a content collection from anywhere at build time. A small custom loader (about 20 lines) would call the GitHub API, fetch your gists (for example, the ones whose filename starts with `article-`), and hand their Markdown to the same pages that exist now. Visitors and search engines still get plain HTML on `saranatour.dev`, so SEO stays the same.

Fetching the gist in the browser instead would hurt SEO and make every page depend on GitHub being up, so I'd rule that out.

## What changes

- **Publishing no longer goes through a PR.** Editing a gist doesn't trigger a deploy, so you'd need a Cloudflare deploy hook. You'd either call it by hand or set up a GitHub Action on a schedule to rebuild.
- **The build depends on GitHub.** The site already fetches your pinned repos at build time, and every build here has logged "Bad credentials" and fallen back to a hardcoded list. For articles, a failed fetch must stop the build. Otherwise a deploy could quietly publish the site with no articles.
- **Audio still needs R2.** Gists are meant for text, so the MP3s can't usefully live there. The small `.vtt` timing files could go in the same gist as the article.
- **Drafts get awkward.** Secret gists aren't private: anyone with the link can read them. A draft would be a gist the loader skips, plus a flag you'd have to remember to flip.
- **Duplicate content.** A public gist is a second public copy of each article. The canonical link on your site tells search engines which copy is the original, but secret gists avoid the duplicate entirely.

## My take

Gists are worth it if you want to write and publish from anywhere, like your phone or the GitHub web editor, without opening a PR. They cost you a deploy hook, a token that has to keep working, and articles split across two places.

You said you wanted one PR per article. Keeping them in the repo already gives you that, with review, history and a preview build, and with nothing outside the repo that can break. You can also write in GitHub's web editor and open the PR from there, which covers most of the "write from anywhere" benefit.

If you still want gists, I can build the loader and the deploy hook.

content.text:
I'd commit articles straight to `main`. Your `main` branch isn't protected, so a push goes through without a PR and triggers the deploy. That needs no new tools or accounts; the only thing that changes is your habit.

## Day to day

**Text-only article:** write it wherever is handy and commit it to `main`.
- On your laptop: add `src/content/articles/my-post.md`, then `git commit` and `git push`.
- From your phone or browser: on github.com, open `src/content/articles/`, click **Add file → Create new file**, write the article, and choose **Commit directly to the main branch**.

**Narrated article:** this one needs your laptop anyway, because marking the timings happens in `pnpm dev` with the audio file. Follow the same steps as before, then push to `main` instead of opening a PR.

## What still protects you without a PR

- **`draft: true`** lets you commit unfinished articles to `main` without them showing up. Flip it to `false` when it's ready.
- **A broken build doesn't take the site down.** If an article has bad frontmatter, the Cloudflare build fails and the site stays as it was. You'd only notice in the Cloudflare dashboard or GitHub's commit status, so glance at it after pushing.

## When something else makes sense

- **You want a writing app, not a file editor:** a Git-based CMS like Pages CMS gives you a web editor with fields for title, date and draft, and saves each article as a commit to `main`. It's free and needs one config file in the repo. I'd only add it if editing Markdown on GitHub starts to feel like friction.
- **You want to write somewhere outside GitHub entirely**, like Notion or gists: that's the build-time loader plus deploy hook I described before. It's more moving parts, and I wouldn't do it just to avoid PRs.

## One related thing

Before the first article, the articles feature itself still needs to land on `main`. It's sitting uncommitted on `add-articles`. I'd do that one as a PR, since it touches shared files like `BaseHead` and the nav. The guide in `docs/publishing-articles.md` also currently says "one article per PR"; it should be rewritten for pushing straight to `main`.

Narrated articles now get a custom player bar in place of the browser's default one. It sits under the description and stays stuck to the top of the screen while you scroll.

You didn't have a reference, so I went with a podcast-style pill in your site's colors:

- **Speed:** a small pill on the right that cycles 1x → 1.25x → 1.5x → 2x.

The speed pill shows "x" rather than "×" because your Recoleta demo font doesn't have the × character and drew a broken glyph.

## How to do the Krisp version

Krisp cleans your microphone live, so anything you record through it is already the cleaned version. The catch is that the site uses one timings file for both versions. So the clean and original files need identical pauses, which in practice means they must come from the same take.

**Option 1: record both versions at once.** This is the way to keep using Krisp.
1. Open **Audio MIDI Setup** on your Mac, click **+**, and choose **Create Aggregate Device**.
2. Tick your real microphone and **Krisp Microphone**.
3. In Audacity or GarageBand, record from that aggregate device. You get two tracks of the same take: one raw, one cleaned by Krisp.
4. Export the Krisp track as `my-post.mp3` and the raw track as `my-post.original.mp3`, then set `originalAudio: true`.

**Option 2: skip Krisp and clean afterwards.** This is simpler.
1. Record once, with Krisp off, and save that as `my-post.original.mp3`.
2. Make the clean copy from that file with a noise remover that doesn't change timing, for example Audacity's **Effect → Noise Removal**. Save it as `my-post.mp3`.

Either way, record the timings once on `my-post.mp3`; the original reuses them. Check that whatever cleans the audio doesn't remove silences, or the highlight will drift on one of the two versions.

If you'll only ever publish the clean version, leave `originalAudio` off and the switch won't appear.

content.text:
Each article now gets its own OG image, title, description and SEO tags, plus several things that help AI answer engines. The build, type-check and tests pass, and I checked the generated HTML for your first article. None of it is committed yet.

**Its own OG image**
- Each article gets a 1200×630 share card generated at build time, styled like your existing ones: black background, thin frame lines, Inter. It shows the title, description, date and reading time, and "With audio" when the article is narrated. The first one is at `/og/articles/i-write-articles-now.png`.
- LinkedIn, X, Discord and others all use that card for the article. Other pages keep your current images.

**SEO tags on each article page**
- **Title and description:** "Title | Sara Natour", and the article's own description.
- **Canonical and Open Graph:** canonical URL, `og:type` set to `article`, and the image's size and alt text.
- **Dates and topics:** `article:published_time`, plus two new optional frontmatter fields:
  - `updatedDate`: becomes `article:modified_time`.
  - `tags`: becomes `article:tag` and the keywords in the structured data.

**For AI answer engines**
- **Structured data** for search engines, describing the article:
  - author with your LinkedIn and GitHub
  - word count and reading time
  - published and updated dates
  - where it was shared, and the audio file when narrated
  - a Home › Articles › title breadcrumb
- **Articles list:** structured data marking it as your blog and listing every article. It also has a fuller description; I wrote it, so edit it in [src/pages/articles/index.astro](src/pages/articles/index.astro).
- **Markdown copies:** every page now links to its Markdown copy, which your site already generates and AI tools read most easily.
- **llms.txt:** it now lists every published article, generated at build, so it never goes stale. The hand-written part moved to [src/llms.txt](src/llms.txt), and you edit it the same way as before.

**Things to know**
- **New dependencies:** `satori` and `sharp` to draw the cards, plus two Inter font files in `src/assets/fonts/`.
- **Your social links** in the structured data come from the `PUBLIC_LINKEDIN` and `PUBLIC_GITHUB` environment variables. Your local `.env` has them. If Cloudflare's build doesn't set them, live pages just leave those links out.
Commit and push
